background: Indiana native who began as a student manager under Bob Knight at Indiana, then spent nearly two decades as a college assistant (USC Upstate, Murray State, Eastern Michigan, UAB, Louisiana Tech, Florida under Mike White). Head coach at Florida Atlantic 2018-24 (126-69), including the 2023 Final Four run (35-4) and a 2024 NCAA bid. Hired by Michigan in March 2024; went 27-10 with a Big Ten Tournament title and Sweet 16 in 2024-25, then 37-3 with a Big Ten regular-season title (record 19-1), Big Ten Coach of the Year and the 2026 NCAA championship (beat UConn 69-63). Hired by the Mavericks on June 23, 2026 (reported June 22), two weeks after Masai Ujiri took over basketball operations and Jason Kidd departed; his first NBA job of any kind. Known for up-tempo, free-flowing, analytics-informed offense built around rim pressure and 3-point volume, switch-heavy defense, two-big lineups and an empowering, 'teacher' style rather than in-game micromanagement.

key_criticisms: No NBA experience at any level; untested in managing veteran stars, 82-game load management, challenges and NBA late-game rules.
Early tension between his two-big preferences and his up-tempo identity (2024).
Mavericks' 3-point shooting personnel is a question for a coach whose system depends on volume (2026 preview).
Analyst framing of him as a teacher rather than an in-game tactician raises ATO/clutch uncertainty.
key_strengths: Elite program builder: Final Four at FAU (2023) and a national title in year two at Michigan (2026).
Modern, analytics-informed offense: pace, rim pressure, 3-point volume, read-based ball movement.
Player development and empowerment culture; strong fit with a young franchise star (Flagg).
Adapts scheme to personnel (switch vs rim-protect; two-big vs five-out).
